newsitem.title: USA: Dlr ends modestly lower in U.S. ahead of Tues FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Dlr ends modestly lower in U.S. ahead of Tues FOMC.

text.p: The dollar inched lower in U.S. trade against most major currencies on Monday before trading ground to a halt ahead of a critical meeting of U.S. monetary policymakers set for Tuesday, currency dealers said.
In an otherwise lacklustre session, a sharp rally in the British pound lent support to the dollar, especially against the mark as investors bought pounds for marks.
Growing prospects for a rise in U.S. short-term interest rates at Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting also aided the U.S. currency, dealers said.
However, nervousness over a possible downturn in worldwide stock and bond markets Tuesday if U.S. interest rates are raised dragged down the dollar by the close of U.S. trade.
"It will be important to see how the other markets react to what the Federal Reserve does or does not do," said Bob Near, a vice president at the Bank of New York.
"The most likely reaction tomorrow is a market selloff -- buy the rumor, sell the fact," he added.
Higher interest rates typically serve as a brake on the speed of economic growth and make the domestic currency more attractive to investors.

Foreign exchange experts widely expect the FOMC to raise the federal funds rate by 25 basis points Tuesday to 5.50 percent from 5.25 percent, which would be the first rise by the Committee in more than two years.
Currency dealers said they have already incorporated this expectation into the dollar's current trading level.
The market virtually ignored comments from German Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke, who addressed the troubling overseas ramifications of higher U.S. rates.
Welteke was quoted by German radio saying he hoped the United States would not raise rates for as long as possible, or German interest rates might move higher, which "cannot be desireable".
The dollar inched lower to 1.6882/87 marks by Monday's close from 1.6900/05 at the open and 122.95/00 yen from 123.03/08.
The British pound rose broadly after news of healthy fourth-quarter UK economic growth and a sharp improvement in the UK trade balance.
British gross domestic prodcut expanded by 0.8 percent in the fourth quarter and the UK posted a current account surplus of 873 million pounds in the same period.
"We saw good buying of sterling. The numbers that came out were on the strong side and that added to the rally today," said Seth Garrett, chief dealer at Credit Suisse First Boston.

Sterling hit a $1.6215 high before closing at $1.6192/02 from $1.6090/00 at Monday's open. The dollar fell to 1.4582/87 Swiss francs from 1.4605/15 and rose to Canadian $1.3785/90 from C$1.3750/55. The Australian dollar rose to $0.7896/01 from $0.7865/70 Friday. ((--Roanne Daniels, 212-859-1677))
